title: Adding min()/max()/sum()/avg() aggregates wrapped the caller-supplied column name in sqlalchemy.text() with no check that it is a real model field, so a crafted column string injects SQL into the aggregate query.

findings.explanation: The diff does not contain any SQL query construction or string interpolation with user input. The changes are all within the ormar ORM framework (decorators, field definitions, model helpers) and example documentation. ORM frameworks typically handle parameterization internally, and no raw SQL strings are constructed from user input in this diff.

The diff does not modify any endpoint handlers, access control checks, or authorization logic. The changes consist of: (1) adding new signal decorators for relation events (pre_relation_add, post_relation_add, etc.), (2) adding ordering parameters to field definitions (orders_by, related_orders_by), (3) refactoring validation logic into a helper function, and (4) model metadata initialization. None of these changes involve fetching objects by user-controlled IDs, checking object ownership, or protecting operations, so no authorization flaws are introduced.
